## Overview

The adventuring classes of Kythoria represent the diverse ways in which mortals harness skill, magic, and inner strength to survive, reclaim, and shape their world. In a civilization forged by two centuries of ongoing reconquering, class is not merely a profession — it is a calling, a discipline, and in many cases, a direct relationship with the cosmic forces that underpin existence itself.

Every class in Kythoria, whether martial or magical, draws ultimately from the same foundational truth: **the arcane energy of B's Great Sacrifice suffuses all creation**. The difference between a wizard and a cleric, a monk and a sorcerer, lies not in the nature of the power they wield, but in the **path through which they access it**.

---

## Principles of Class Power

### The Unified Source

All magic in Kythoria traces back to the **Great Sacrifice**, when B — one of the three Originals — scattered their essence across all planes of existence. This arcane energy became:

- **The Weave** — a network of magic that can be studied, shaped, and manipulated through formulae and will
- **Nature's Absorption** — the natural world soaked up residual energy, making it accessible through attunement to the wild
- **Inner Resonance** — every living being carries a fragment of this energy within themselves
- **Divine Conduits** — the gods (fragments of A and C) act as channels, filtering this energy to their faithful

### The Paths to Power

| Path | Mechanism | Classes |
|------|-----------|---------|
| **Weave Manipulation** | Direct study and manipulation of the arcane network through formulae, ritual, and intelligence | Wizard, Artificer |
| **Weave + Inner Expression** | Harnessing innate arcane resonance shaped by artistic expression and performance | Bard |
| **Divine Channeling** | Prayer and devotion through the gods, who act as conduits for arcane energy | Cleric |
| **Oath-Sworn Channeling** | A sacred oath sworn to a god, who validates and channels power through the paladin's conviction | Paladin |
| **Primal Attunement** | Drawing absorbed energy directly from the natural world | Druid, Ranger |
| **Innate Bloodline** | A specific ancestral exposure to raw arcane energy, passed through generations | Sorcerer |
| **Pact Bond** | A direct bargain with an entity capable of granting arcane energy | Warlock |
| **Inner Ki** | Introspective meditation discovering the arcane energy within all living beings | Monk |
| **Pure Discipline** | Martial training, physical conditioning, and tactical skill — no spells | Fighter, Rogue, Barbarian |

---

## The Classes of Kythoria

### Artificer

**Source of Power:** Weave manipulation through technical skill and craftsmanship.

**Cultural Perception:** Highly respected as the wisest of crafters. Artificers combine smithing, engineering, and arcane theory to create magical items, infused weapons, and mechanical marvels. They are especially valued in **Emberforge**, where the **Thormvuld family** — dwarven arcane engineers — are the continent's premier producers of magical equipment. The frontier also holds artificers in high regard, as their creations extend the reach of civilization into monster-held territory.

**Training:** Formal apprenticeship under a master artificer, typically through a guild. The **Thormvuld workshops** (south of the northeast settlement cluster) and **Emberforge's engineering houses** are the premier training grounds.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Battle Smith** — Common in Emberforge, producing combat constructs for the Last Stand military
- **Artillerist** — Frontier specialists who create defensive turrets for outposts
- **Armorer** — Emberforge's elite armorers who outfit high-ranking officers

*(Note: Artificer NPCs will not appear in early campaign content — the DM is becoming familiar with the class.)*

---

### Barbarian

**Source of Power:** Primal fury, physical discipline, and connection to ancestral traditions. Barbarians do not cast spells, but their rage taps into something deep — perhaps the instinctive survival drive of mortals forged by the Abominable End.

**Cultural Perception:** Barbarians are respected as formidable warriors. They are most common among the **four great tribes**, one in each cardinal direction, whose traditions predate the monster invasion. These tribes maintain their own customs, oral histories, and ways of war. (Details of these tribes are tied to a player character's backstory and will be expanded later.)

**Training:** Tribal tradition, survival in the wild, or military service as shock troops. Some barbarians are frontier folk who developed their rage through years of fighting monsters with nothing but steel and will.

**Regional Distribution:**
- **Northern tribe** — Frozen tundra, facing the worst of the monster hordes
- **Southern tribe** — Subtropical jungles, guardians of ancient ruins
- **Eastern tribe** — Coastal, seafaring traditions
- **Western tribe** — Frontier, most actively engaged in reconquering

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Path of the Berserker** — Common across all four tribes
- **Path of the Totem Warrior** — Each tribe reveres different animal spirits aligned to their environment
- **Path of the Ancestral Guardian** — Tribal elders who channel the spirits of fallen ancestors

---

### Bard

**Source of Power:** A blend of innate arcane energy (present in all living beings) and deliberate Weave manipulation, expressed through artistic performance. Bards do not study magic from books — they *feel* it, shape it through music, poetry, and storytelling, and channel it through their art.

**Cultural Perception:** Highly respected as keepers of history, morale-boosters, and weavers of influence. Bards are the living memory of the mortal races, preserving songs, epics, and records that survived the Abominable End. They serve as diplomats, spies, entertainers, and chroniclers. A well-regarded bard can walk into any court in Kythoria.

**Training:** Apprenticeship with an established bard, or study at an academy. Bards often travel extensively, collecting stories and techniques from across the continent.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **College of Lore** — Centered in **Weaveheart**, bards who study ancient texts and arcane knowledge alongside their art
- **College of Valor** — Common in **Skywatch**, bards who accompany military expeditions and compose war epics
- **College of Swords** — Frontier bards who blend performance with blade-work, entertaining taverns from the heartlands to the edge of civilization

---

### Cleric

**Source of Power:** Divine channeling. Clerics pray to their god, and the god — acting as a conduit for the arcane energy of B's sacrifice — grants them power. **Clerics do not know this.** They believe, as their church teaches, that the power comes directly from the divine will of their god. The gods maintain this deception carefully.

**Cultural Perception:** Pillars of their communities. Clerics are trusted, revered, and sought after for healing, guidance, and protection. Every settlement of any size has at least one temple or shrine tended by a cleric. They are the most visible face of the divine in daily life.

**Training:** Formal religious education at a temple or seminary run by their church. Clerics of different gods train separately, though the **Ecumenical Council** facilitates some cross-faith study.

**Military Role:** Clerics are essential in the Last Stand's army — frontline healers and divine support who keep soldiers alive in monster territory.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Life Domain** — The most common. Temples of the Order of the Dawn (God of Light and Life)
- **Forge Domain** — Emberforge's Guild of the Spark. Smith-priests who bless weapons and armor
- **Nature Domain** — The Circle of the Wild (God of Nature and Tempest). Frontier and rural temples
- **Order Domain** — The Order of the Scales (God of Wisdom and Justice). Judges and lawkeepers
- **Twilight Domain** — The Vigil of the Dusk (God of Peace and Twilight). Guardians of thresholds
- **Trickery Domain** — The Coven of the Spider (Lolth). Rare, practiced in secret
- **Death Domain** — The Order of the Raven (The Raven Queen). Guardians of death rites

---

### Druid

**Source of Power:** Primal attunement. Nature absorbed residual arcane energy from B's sacrifice across millennia. Druids learn to sense, commune with, and draw upon this energy from the natural world — the forests, rivers, mountains, and skies of Kythoria.

**Cultural Perception:** Respected, especially on the frontier. Druids are seen as wise custodians of the wild, essential allies in understanding and navigating monster-controlled territories. Some are reclusive, living in ancient groves far from civilization. Others actively support the reconquering by shaping terrain, scouting through animal forms, and restoring lands damaged by monster presence.

**Training:** Mentorship with an established druid. Druidic circles are loose affiliations of nature-attuned individuals who share knowledge and protect sacred sites. Some circles date back to pre-invasion times.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Circle of the Land** — The most common. Different environments produce different sub-circles (forest, mountain, coast, swamp)
- **Circle of the Moon** — Frontier druids who master wild shape for combat and scouting
- **Circle of Stars** — Rare. Druids who read the stars and draw power from celestial patterns, possibly connected to the cosmology of Aetris

---

### Fighter

**Source of Power:** Pure martial discipline. Fighters rely on training, strength, endurance, and tactical skill. No magic — just steel and will.

**Cultural Perception:** The backbone of the Last Stand's military. Fighters are common, respected, and essential. Every settlement has veterans who train the next generation. A fighter who has served on the frontier or in a major campaign carries immense social weight.

**Training:** Military service, formal drilling, apprenticeship to a veteran, or self-training. The **Skywatch War College** produces some of the finest tactical fighters, but most learn through experience.

**Military Role:** Fighters form the core of the Last Stand's army. They are the line-holders, the shield-walls, the cavalry, and the skirmishers. No campaign succeeds without them.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Battle Master** — Common among officers and veterans
- **Champion** — Common among rank-and-file soldiers
- **Eldritch Knight** — Rare. Fighters who supplement martial skill with basic Weave study, often trained in Weaveheart
- **Cavalier** — Skywatch's mounted scouts and cavalry units

---

### Monk

**Source of Power:** Inner Ki. Millennia ago — long before the monster invasion — certain mortals began to meditate introspectively, seeking a deeper understanding of themselves and the world. Through generations of disciplined practice, they discovered that **every living being carries a fragment of arcane energy within**. They called this energy **Ki**. It is, in truth, the same arcane energy of B's sacrifice that permeates all existence, but reached through inner stillness rather than external study.

**Cultural Perception:** A rare sight in Kythoria. Monastic traditions are ancient — pre-invasion — and many monasteries were destroyed during the Abominable End. Surviving monks are wandering figures, viewed with a mixture of curiosity and deep respect. Their discipline is admired, their philosophy often misunderstood.

**Training:** Intensive training at a monastery (now rare) or under a wandering master. Some monks train alone, having discovered their inner Ki through perseverance and meditation without formal instruction.

**Military Role:** Monks serve in the Last Stand's army as elite skirmishers and scouts. Their speed, precision, and ability to fight without weapons or armor makes them valuable in monster territory where equipment can be lost or compromised.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Way of the Open Hand** — The most traditional monastic discipline
- **Way of Shadow** — Rare. Monks who walk the boundary between light and dark. Some may have discovered connections to the Shadowfell
- **Way of the Sun Soul** — Extremely rare. Monks who channel Ki as radiant energy. Possibly connected to the God of Light and Life, or simply a manifestation of pure life-energy

---

### Paladin

**Source of Power:** Oath-sworn channeling. A paladin swears a sacred oath **to a god**, binding their will and purpose to a divine ideal. The god validates the oath and serves as the conduit. But the power itself flows through the paladin's **conviction** — their unshakeable adherence to the tenets of their oath.

This is distinct from a cleric's prayer-based channeling:
- **Clerics** maintain an ongoing relationship of devotion — they pray, and their god answers
- **Paladins** swear an oath once, and the power flows as long as they uphold it. The god is the witness and anchor, not the daily interlocutor

If a paladin breaks their oath, the god may sever the connection — though the paladin could theoretically swear anew to a different god, or (in extremely rare and heretical cases) swear to an ideal alone.

**Cultural Perception:** Respected as holy warriors. Paladins are the military arm of faith — more martially focused than clerics, more divinely grounded than fighters. They serve as commanders, champions, and moral exemplars. A paladin's word is generally trusted throughout Kythoria.

**Training:** Combined military and religious education. Many paladins train at their church's martial academies or at the **Skywatch War College**, supplementing their religious studies with military tactics.

**Military Role:** Paladins are frontline commanders and elite warriors in the Last Stand's army. Their presence inspires troops and their divine smites are devastating against monsters.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Oath of Devotion** — God of Light and Life. The most common paladin oath
- **Oath of the Crown** — God of Wisdom and Justice. Paladins who serve the Council Accord and the laws of civilization
- **Oath of Vengeance** — Common across multiple gods. Paladins dedicated to hunting specific monsters or threats
- **Oath of Conquest** — Rare. Paladins focused on the total destruction of monster-held territories
- **Oath of Redemption** — God of Peace and Twilight. Rare. Paladins who believe even monsters can be saved

---

### Ranger

**Source of Power:** Primal attunement combined with martial skill. Like druids, rangers draw on nature's absorbed arcane energy — but they blend it with practical survival training, tracking, and ranged combat.

**Cultural Perception:** Essential for survival. Rangers are the eyes and ears of the frontier, the guides through monster territory, and the hunters who track threats before they reach settled lands. They are deeply respected, especially in **Skywatch** and along the **Frontier Road**.

**Training:** Apprenticeship to an experienced ranger, or self-taught through years of frontier survival. The **Scouts' & Rangers' Guild** headquartered in Skywatch provides formal training and certification.

**Military Role:** Rangers serve as scouts, skirmishers, and monster-trackers in the Last Stand's army. They operate ahead of main forces, mapping terrain and identifying threats.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Hunter** — The standard frontier ranger, trained to track and eliminate specific monster types
- **Gloom Stalker** — Rare. Rangers who operate in the deep frontier, in shadow, or even near the Shadowfell
- **Beast Master** — Rangers who bond with animal companions, common among frontier and tribal traditions

---

### Rogue

**Source of Power:** Skill, stealth, and cunning. Rogues rely on training, agility, and a willingness to operate in the shadows. No magic (usually) — just expertise.

**Cultural Perception:** Complex. Rogues are essential to society — as scouts, spies, information-brokers, and (inevitably) the primary operatives of the **black market**. They are respected out of fear and necessity, but rarely trusted. A known rogue can find work anywhere but friendship nowhere.

**Training:** Apprenticeship to a senior rogue, or self-taught through street survival. Some rogues are former soldiers who developed unconventional skills on the frontier. Others are guild-trained in lockpicking, trap-disabling, and information-gathering.

**Military Role:** Rogues are rare in the formal military. When they serve, it is as scouts, saboteurs, or intelligence operatives — often operating independently or in small specialist units.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Thief** — The most common. Street-operators, trap-disarmers, treasure-hunters in ruins
- **Assassin** — Rare. Operatives who eliminate high-value targets. Some serve the Coven of the Spider (Lolth)
- **Scout** — Common in Skywatch. Rogues who blend stealth with wilderness survival
- **Arcane Trickster** — Rare. Rogues who supplement their skills with basic Weave manipulation

---

### Sorcerer

**Source of Power:** Innate bloodline. A sorcerer's power comes from within — a specific ancestor was exposed to raw arcane energy, and that exposure passed down through generations, manifesting as an innate magical talent. The cause is always unique to the individual or bloodline: a dragon's blessing, exposure to a planar rift, contact with an arcane-reactive crystal, descent from a being touched by wild magic.

**Cultural Perception:** Viewed with curiosity and mistrust. People fear what they do not understand, and sorcerers are walking embodiments of uncontrollable magic. Unlike wizards (who studied for their power) or clerics (whose power comes from a known god), sorcerers simply *have* power — and that makes people uneasy. A sorcerer must earn trust through deeds.

**Training:** Largely self-taught. Sorcerers cannot be trained in the traditional sense — their power is innate, not learned. However, many seek out mentors (often wizards or older sorcerers) who can help them understand and control their abilities. The **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts** accepts sorcerers for supplementary education.

**Military Role:** Sorcerers are rare in the formal military. Those who serve are valued for their raw magical power but often viewed as unpredictable assets.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **Draconic Bloodline** — Descendants of ancient dragons (who may or may not still exist in Aetris)
- **Wild Magic** — Those whose bloodline was touched by raw, unstable arcane energy — possibly from the barrier's creation or from arcane-reactive crystal exposure
- **Shadow Magic** — Those connected to the Shadowfell. Extremely rare on the Material Plane
- **Divine Soul** — Those whose bloodline was touched by divine energy — a claim the churches watch carefully

---

### Warlock

**Source of Power:** Pact bond. A warlock makes a direct bargain with an entity capable of granting arcane energy. The patron provides power; the warlock provides service, tribute, or adherence to certain terms. The exact nature of the pact varies wildly.

**Critical Cosmology Note:** The **Originals no longer exist** — B is scattered, A and C subdivided into the gods. They cannot be warlock patrons. However, the Weave and the arcane energy of B's sacrifice have enabled **any sufficiently powerful entity** to make pacts and grant power. Patrons can include:

- **Archfey** from the Feywild
- **Fiends** from the Nine Hells
- **Great Old Ones** from the Far Realm
- **Celestials** from the Upper Planes
- **The Raven Queen** (or aspects of her domain)
- **Lolth** (who occasionally makes pacts beyond her drow followers)
- **Other planar entities** both known and unknown

**The Divine Pantheon's Blind Spot:** The gods do not know all warlock patrons. They *can* investigate — by following the Weave's threads back to the patron entity — but they rarely bother unless a warlock's patron grows powerful enough to threaten their influence.

**Secret:** *(GM knowledge)* A large cluster of B's crystal, deep beneath the continent, may have achieved sentience. If it has begun making pacts with warlocks, it would be a secret that threatens the entire divine pantheon's authority — for it would prove that B's essence, believed scattered and dead, is stirring.

**Cultural Perception:** Viewed with deep mistrust and respect born of fear. Making a deal with an unknown entity is dangerous and, to most mortals, morally questionable. Warlocks are tolerated when their power is useful and their patron seems benign, but they are watched carefully. A warlock whose patron is discovered to be a fiend or darker entity may face ostracism or worse.

**Training:** There is no formal training for warlocks. The pact itself grants knowledge and power. Some warlocks seek out others of their kind for guidance, but each pact is unique.

**Military Role:** Warlocks are very rare in the formal military. When they serve, they are typically kept at arm's length — too useful to dismiss, too dangerous to fully trust.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **The Archfey** — Pacts with fey entities from the Feywild. Seen as unpredictable but not inherently evil
- **The Fiend** — Pacts with infernal powers. Viewed with great suspicion
- **The Great Old One** — Pacts with entities from beyond known reality. Barely understood, deeply feared
- **The Celestial** — Pacts with benevolent celestial beings. Rare — the gods watch these closely
- **The Hexblade** — Pacts with sentient weapons or shadowy entities from the Shadowfell

---

### Wizard

**Source of Power:** Weave manipulation through study. Wizards learn the language of magic — formulae, gestures, components — and shape the Weave through disciplined intellect.

**Cultural Perception:** Respected and valued, especially in **Weaveheart**, where the **Academy of Arcane Arts** is the continent's premier magical institution. Wizards are seen as scholars and professionals — magic as a science rather than a mystery. A wizard's title and specialization carry weight in academic and political circles.

**Training:** Formal education at an academy or apprenticeship to a master wizard. The **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts** is the most prestigious, but smaller schools and individual mentors exist throughout the recovered territories.

**Military Role:** Wizards serve in the Last Stand's army as battle-mages, siege specialists, and barrier maintenance experts. Weaveheart supplies the bulk of military wizards.

**Common Subclasses (Cultural Traditions):**
- **School of Evocation** — Last Stand military mages. Masters of destructive magic
- **School of Abjuration** — Barrier specialists. Ward-crafters and defensive mages
- **School of Divination** — Skywatch's intelligence mages. Scouts and information-gatherers
- **School of Conjuration** — Frontier support mages who summon creatures and transport supplies
- **School of Illusion** — Weaveheart's entertainers and spies
- **School of Transmutation** — Emberforge's industrial mages who shape materials and enhance forging
- **War Magic** — Elite military wizards who blend evocation with tactical awareness

## The Last Stand Army — Class Composition

The unified military of the three capitals draws from all classes, but in different proportions:

| Role | Common Classes | Notes |
|------|---------------|-------|
| **Frontline** | Fighter, Paladin, Barbarian, Monk | The shield and hammer of the army |
| **Support** | Cleric, Druid, Ranger | Healing, scouting, terrain control |
| **Arcane Corps** | Wizard, Artificer | Battle-magic, equipment, barrier maintenance |
| **Rare** | Sorcerer, Warlock, Rogue | Too unpredictable, too rare, or too distrusted for standard deployment |

---

## Training & Class Acquisition

### Formal Institutions

| Institution | Location | Classes Trained |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts** | Weaveheart | Wizard, Sorcerer (supplementary), Bard (supplementary) |
| **Skywatch War College** | Skywatch | Fighter, Paladin, Ranger, strategic officers |
| **Emberforge Engineering Halls** | Emberforge | Artificer |
| **Church Seminaries** | All three capitals | Cleric, Paladin (religious education) |
| **Scouts' & Rangers' Guild** | Skywatch | Ranger, Rogue (scout path) |

### Informal Training

- **Apprenticeship** — Artificers, Bards, Rogues, Wizards
- **Mentorship** — Druids, Monks, Rangers
- **Self-taught** — Sorcerers, Warlocks, some Rogues and Barbarians
- **Tribal tradition** — Barbarians, some Druids and Rangers
- **Military service** — Fighters, Paladins, some Wizards and Clerics

## The Adventurers' Guild & Classes

The continent-wide **Adventurers' Guild** (name TBD) does not restrict membership by class. Adventurers of all classes are welcome. The guild organizes, coordinates, and supports adventuring activity across the recovered territories. Its internal structure, rank system, and relationship to specific classes will be defined when the guild is detailed as a separate entity.

---

## Cultural Significance

Adventuring classes in Kythoria are more than professions — they are **expressions of the mortal response to a world under siege**. Each class represents a different answer to the same question: *How do we survive, reclaim, and build a future?*

- The **fighter** says: through discipline and steel.
- The **cleric** says: through faith and community.
- The **wizard** says: through knowledge and understanding.
- The **druid** says: through harmony with the land.
- The **monk** says: through mastery of the self.
- The **warlock** says: through bold bargains and risk.
- The **rogue** says: through adaptability and cunning.
- The **barbarian** says: through ancestral strength and primal will.
- The **sorcerer** says: through the power within.
- The **paladin** says: through sacred purpose.
- The **ranger** says: through survival and vigilance.
- The **artificer** says: through creation and ingenuity.

Together, they form the mosaic of mortal capability — each path valid, each needed. The reconquering would fail without any of them.
